scope: Tracked source at this revision; source-only registration candidates, not a running router or a vulnerability scan.
limitations: HTTP registration paths are local source arguments. Constructor prefixes, caller mounts, loops, .all() expansion, implicit HEAD, conditional routes, and framework/plugin-owned routes require composition review.

Method-name scanning can include non-router calls with the same signature; computed arguments remain explicitly unresolved. Non-path-like computed calls are retained separately in excludedMethodCalls for manual recheck.
Canonical registry and mutation/mint tables are discovery cross-checks, not independent evidence that every live route enforces its classification.
Browser routeId includes TanStack pathless/layout conventions and is not necessarily the public URL.
Source file counts exclude tests/fixtures/declarations and generated route trees; they do not measure audit depth or security coverage.

tokenMintCensus.note: Standing-only mint: no boundary composes and an elevation token is refused, so no grant can confer; the `token_mint` step-up-only designation gates it all the same.

The elevation token mint: the product IS the grant-bound credential (`tokens.elevation_grant_id`, the grant scope, the grant window), so no clamp question arises; the activation proof the mint itself demands is the ceremony, so no separate step-up designation gates it.

The `sds_` connection family: elevation never confers a SCIM mint (no `token_mint` boundary composes) and the step-up-only designation governs the `sdp_` credential family, so the columns read as the refusal pair alone.
Rotation mints a fresh bearer secret for the connection — the create route’s answers apply unchanged.

The `sdf_` fact-push family: elevation never confers a fact-push mint (no `token_mint` boundary composes — the mint demands an unscoped standing credential and refuses every non-null scope outright) and the step-up-only designation governs the `sdp_` credential family, so the columns read as the refusal pair alone.
Rotation mints a fresh `sdf_` bearer for the push token — the create route’s answers apply unchanged.
Standing-only mint (the npm legacy login); the `token_mint` step-up-only designation gates it through the registry-api’s standalone gate.
Standing-only mint (the npm v1 token API); the `token_mint` step-up-only designation gates it through the registry-api’s standalone gate.

The stateless docker registry-token mint. The realm’s credential surface is HTTP Basic with an `sdp_` password (standard, entitlement, or elevation-bound) or anonymous — never a Bearer JWT: the auth seam’s path predicate excludes `/v2/token` exactly (`dockerStatelessCredentialAppliesToPath`), so a JWT presented there falls through `verifyToken` as the unknown credential it is, and the realm handler additionally refuses any JWT signed by a key in the Docker token keyring, whatever its issuer — both arms answer the standing 401 + Basic challenge, and no re-mint is possible. The product is therefore always a 300 s signature over the intersection of an `sdp_` caller’s standing grants AND token-scope envelope with the requested scopes (anonymous: the unambiguous-`anonymousRead` pull set) — no row is persisted, so no grant can bind the product and there is no `minted_under_grant_id` (the data-path capability guard is the binding, and principal state re-resolves fresh per request). A credential whose authority the stateless JWT cannot represent is echoed verbatim, never minted from — echoing confers nothing (the operation boundary still pins the grant; the data path re-verifies the `sdp_` bearer per request) while a minted JWT would launder what the credential carries: an elevation-bound `sdp_` credential (the grant’s time-box would detach from the borrowed authority), an entitlement token (the scope-free data-path reconstruction cannot re-resolve the synthetic principal), any grant-dependent `sdp_` bearer including the repository-wide manufactured ordinary token (`mintedUnderGrantId` or an inherited dependency set — the JWT would strip the per-request dependency-liveness proof the current credential contract’s verification runs), any package-restricted bearer (the JWT reconstruction carries `scopes: null` and would drop the `packages` dimension), and any trusted-publishing token, repository-wide or package-narrowed (a fresh 300 s JWT would outlive the exchanged credential’s original expiry and erase its provenance, even when exchanged moments before that expiry — the echoed bearer keeps revalidating its own expiry and scope per request). Independent standing credentials keep the normal JWT exchange, and a scope outside the caller’s envelope grants nothing — the data path refuses the wider capability request. The OCI token flow defines no step-up re-auth path, so the step-up-only designation never applies. The per-request scope fan-out is bounded: `parseDockerTokenScopes` deduplicates scopes by (type, name) and caps the parsed list at 64 unique entries (`DOCKER_TOKEN_SCOPE_LIMIT`), and resolution memoizes one repository lookup per unique slug within the request, so neither the mint’s database work nor its audit payload scales with the query string.

The OIDC trusted-publishing exchange — one shared implementation, the `makeTrustedPublishingRoutes` factory, serves every trusted-publishing format’s mount — authenticates the CI vendor’s JWT — no Depot credential presents, so no elevation token can reach the mint and no grant exists to clamp to; a fresh-proof receipt is principal-keyed and there is no principal session to proof. The minted token is bounded by construction (repository-scoped, TTL-capped). The shared implementation’s primitive calls are counted on the canonical pypi row.
